2) Core functionality & requirements mapping - REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION / REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION: - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts implements comment scanning in `create(context) → Program` which calls `processComment` for each comment. - `processComment` and `processCommentLine` detect `@story`, `@req`, and `@supports` tags and manage a `PendingAnnotation` state so syntax is normalized and validated according to the spec. - JSDoc on create() includes `@req REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION - Implement formatting checks per specification` and `@req REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION - Ensure rule create function validates annotations syntax`. - REQ-PATH-FORMAT: - `validateStoryAnnotation(context, comment, rawValue, options)` trims and collapses the value, then: - Treats missing value as a specific error: reports `invalidStoryFormat` with details from `buildStoryErrorMessage("missing", ...)`. - Validates against `options.storyPattern` (default path format `^docs/stories/...\.story\.md$`). - Rejects values with internal whitespace or path traversal (e.g. `../docs/...`) and reports `invalidStoryFormat` with detailed messages. - Uses `getFixedStoryPath` and `reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix` to safely auto-fix missing `.md` / `.story.md` suffixes while preserving surrounding comment text. - JSDoc and inline comments reference `@req REQ-PATH-FORMAT` at the function and branch level. - REQ-REQ-FORMAT: - `validateReqAnnotation(context, comment, rawValue, options)` trims/collapses the value, validates against `options.reqPattern` (default `^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$`), and reports `invalidReqFormat` with details from `buildReqErrorMessage("missing"/"invalid", ...)`. - JSDoc references `@req REQ-REQ-FORMAT - Validate @req identifiers follow expected patterns`. - REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT: - `PendingAnnotation` type and logic in `processCommentLine` and `finalizePendingAnnotation` allow `@story`/`@req` values to span multiple lines within a block/JSDoc comment. - Lines are normalized via `normalizeCommentLine` (src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-format-internal.ts) and concatenated with internal whitespace collapsed before validation. - JSDoc and comments explicitly reference `@req REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT` and describe behavior (do nothing when no pending annotation, extend value across lines, skip blank continuation lines). - REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING: - `normalizeCommentLine` trims whitespace, removes leading `*` from JSDoc lines, and preserves tags `@story`, `@req`, `@supports` even when they appear later in the line, supporting multiple comment styles. - `processCommentLine` ignores empty normalized lines and only starts/extends pending annotations when appropriate. - Code-level annotations reference `@req REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING - Support reasonable variations in whitespace and formatting`. - REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY: - Rule meta messages: `invalidStoryFormat`, `invalidReqFormat`, `invalidImplementsFormat` are all `"Invalid annotation format: {{details}}."`. - `buildStoryErrorMessage` and `buildReqErrorMessage` construct detailed, context-specific `details` strings (e.g., missing path vs invalid path, echoing offending identifier and expected example) used in `context.report({ messageId, data: { details } })`. - docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md documents exact error messages for missing/invalid values, including examples like: - `Missing story path for @story annotation. Expected a path like "docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md".` - `Invalid requirement ID "invalid-format" for @req annotation. Expected an identifier like "REQ-EXAMPLE" (uppercase letters, numbers, and dashes only).`
3) Tests for this story - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts - Uses ESLint RuleTester to exercise the `valid-annotation-format` rule. - Valid cases include: - `[REQ-PATH-FORMAT] valid story annotation format (single-line)` with `// @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md`. - `[REQ-REQ-FORMAT] valid req annotation format (single-line)` with `// @req REQ-EXAMPLE`. - `[REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION] valid block annotations (single-line values)` combining `@story` and `@req` in JSDoc. - `[REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT]` tests for multi-line story and req values split across lines. - `[REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING] valid JSDoc-style comment with leading stars and spacing`. - Invalid cases assert precise messages and, where appropriate, auto-fix output: - `[REQ-PATH-FORMAT] missing story path (single line)` → missing-path details. - `[REQ-PATH-FORMAT] invalid story file extension` and `missing extension in story path` → invalid path details plus expected auto-fixed output. - `[REQ-PATH-FORMAT] story path must not use path traversal` → path traversal is rejected. - `[REQ-REQ-FORMAT]` tests for missing ID, invalid format, and trailing-space variants. - `[REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT]` tests missing/invalid multi-line values after collapsing whitespace. - Additional tests cover configurable patterns and invalid config fallbacks, ensuring robustness and error reporting. - Test run evidence: - `npm test -- --verbose` executed successfully. - Jest output includes: `PASS tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts` with all valid and invalid cases under `Valid Annotation Format Rule (Story 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION)` passing. - Overall: `Test Suites: 35 passed, 35 total` and `Tests: 266 passed, 266 total`.
4) Integration with other rules - src/index.ts - `RULE_NAMES` includes "valid-annotation-format" along with `require-story-annotation`, `require-req-annotation`, and `require-branch-annotation`. - `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES` maps `"traceability/valid-annotation-format": "warn"`, while the other core rules are `"error"`, aligning with error-severity decisions. - `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict` both include this rule via `createTraceabilityFlatConfig()`, so in normal usage it runs alongside the annotation detection rules, satisfying the Integration acceptance criterion.
5) Documentation and UX - docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md - Provides the full format specification for `@story`, `@req`, and `@supports` annotations, including default regex patterns and examples, matching the story’s "Annotation Format Examples" section. - Explains multiline support, flexible parsing, configurable patterns, flat vs nested options, and invalid configuration behavior. - Documents concrete error messages for missing and invalid annotation values and how examples change with configuration, satisfying the User Experience and Documentation acceptance criteria.
6) Error handling and edge cases - Implementation handles: - Empty comments and lines (normalized to "" and ignored). - Missing pending state in finalizePendingAnnotation (returns null safely). - Invalid regex in configuration: meta message `invalidRuleConfiguration` is reported, and code falls back to default patterns while still validating annotations. - Multi-line annotations with missing or invalid values. - Tests include specific cases for invalid regex patterns and ensure both configuration errors and format errors are reported without crashes.
